ideas.description: Exploit: launch the math-preserving I131 base once on seeds 0-2. drafts/I131_base.py is the E082 tip (18 px first stage, 6.875 epochs, block-1 freeze at 0.8, PE-NS3, fused augment, vectorised dirac) plus two additions. (a) I125: a compiled foreach lookahead blend with a 0-d decay tensor, plus a whole-epoch low-res resize for epochs that sit entirely inside one stage. (b) I131: persistent GPU and pinned-host train-set buffers allocated in build(), plus build-time warmups of prepare()'s first-use ops on synthetic data. Both additions were checked bit-identical in unit tests, and neither touches real data or seeds in build(). Before launching, re-run debug_nan.py and check offline that seeds 0-2 per-seed accuracy in one process matches the I131 screen's base config, and that prepare is ~0.02 s on every trial. Launch once and do not re-roll. If it misses, I131_base stays the code base for every later candidate. The recipe's true mean is unchanged, so a miss says nothing about H2.
ideas.expected: Time 4.47-4.54 s, point ~4.50 s (-1.8% vs E082's 4.584 s: outside-step -0.032 s and prepare -0.048 s, both measured offline with synchronized timers). Accuracy is a process-level re-draw around the E082 config's grand mean. Its 20-40-seed means across seven one-process screens are 0.7534-0.7543, about 0.7540 on average. The 3-seed launch sd is ~0.19 pp including the build offset, so P(>=0.753) is ~0.65-0.70. Feasible means a new tip at ~4.50 s. Time above 4.55 s would mean the prepare savings do not carry over to the harness process (check per-trial prepare in the log).

ideas.description: Explore. Proposes a new Lvl1/Lvl2 node, H8: where each block downsamples is the largest untested FLOP lever. ConvGroup runs conv1 BEFORE its max-pool, so the first conv of blocks 2 and 3 runs at 4x the area of the block output. Per image, the 473.8 MFLOP (MAC) total includes block-2 conv1 at 15x15 (128->384, ~99.5 M, 21%) and block-3 conv1 at 7x7 (384->576, ~97.5 M, 21%). Pooling first (x = act(norm1(conv1(pool(x))))) cuts those to ~21.7 M and ~17.9 M while keeping every output and final-map size (2x2 at 18 px, 3x3 at 28/32 px). The residual x0 stays after conv1. Screen in ONE process with one build on seeds 3-42 (40 seeds), arms alternating per seed. Each arm is its own model/graph set, all warmed in build() with channels_last tensors (E035) across every resolution, freeze variant and partial shape, so times are valid. Base: drafts/I131_base.py. Arms: c0 = base. c1 = pool-first in block 3 only. c2 = pool-first in blocks 2 and 3. c3 = pool-first in block 1 only (pool the 31x31 whitening output to 15x15 before block-1 conv1; this removes the memory-bound 31x31x128 BN/SiLU traffic that made I105 slow). c4 = c2's pool-first only in the 18/28 px graphs, with the 32 px graphs unchanged (a curriculum-style cheap early phase; weights are shared). Use static-kernel F.max_pool2d only, never amax (E009). Keep Muon shape groups batched; conv shapes do not change, only input sizes, so the groups are unchanged. Run debug_nan.py on every new graph. Report per arm: 40-seed mean, paired delta vs c0 with SE, offline time, and the price in pp lost per 1% of time saved. Promote to I138 any arm priced <=0.025 pp per 1% (half the ~0.05 frontier) at >=2 SE of time saving. No seeds-0-2 run from this idea.
ideas.expected: c1: FLOPs -17%, time -10% to -14%, paired accuracy -1.5 to -0.2 pp, point -0.6 pp (~0.05 pp per 1%, at the frontier). c2: FLOPs -33%, time -20% to -27%, accuracy -3.0 to -0.8 pp, point -1.6 pp. c3: time -4% to -8% (memory-bound savings), accuracy -1.5 to -0.2 pp, point -0.6 pp. c4: time -4% to -7%, accuracy -0.5 to +0.05 pp, point -0.2 pp. Low-res steps sit in warmup and tolerate low fidelity (H6), so c4 is the arm most likely to beat the frontier. If every arm prices >=0.05 pp per 1%, H8 is refuted: the conv-then-pool layout earns its FLOPs under Muon, as block-1 depth did (E037).

ideas.description: Exploit, conditional on I137 promoting at least one arm (price <=0.025 pp per 1%). Turn the saved time into a margin-funded tip. Base: drafts/I131_base.py with the promoted pool-first arm, or the cheapest-priced arm if several are promoted. Screen in ONE process on seeds 3-42 (40 seeds), configs alternating per seed. c0 = I131 base (control). c1-c3 = the promoted arm at three total epoch counts. The extra epochs go into the 32 px stage. Keep the 18/28 px boundaries (75000, 175000) and the whitening-bias freeze fixed in samples, keep the block-1 freeze at 0.8 of total samples, and index all schedules by samples seen. The final partial epoch uses the matching fraction of its permutation, and the fused augment writes only consumed samples. Choose the epoch values from I137's price and the ~0.9 pp/epoch upward slope (I114) so they bracket the arm's c0-matched accuracy: for c4, about 6.875, 7.0 and 7.125; for c1, about 7.25, 7.5 and 7.75. Warm every new partial shape in build() (E035) and run debug_nan.py. Pre-registered launch rule, as in I130: m = 40-seed mean; t = offline time x (4.50 / the I131 base's offline time, or the E082 calibration if I136 has not run); P = Phi((m - 0.7530)/0.19); EV = P x (current tip time - t). Launch the argmax-EV config once only if P >= 0.65 and t is <= 2% below the current tip. Never re-roll. If I137 promotes nothing, drop this idea.
ideas.expected: If c4 is promoted (e.g. -5% for -0.15 pp): the best config is around 7.0 epochs, t ~4.35-4.42 s, m ~0.7540, P ~0.70, which would be a new tip ~2-3.5% below 4.50. If c1 is promoted: around 7.5 epochs, t ~4.2-4.35 s, m ~0.7538. The chance of a launch given promotion is ~60%. If no config meets the rule, the pool-first saving is real but cannot be turned into accuracy margin at the upward knee slope.

ideas.description: Explore the activation's cost on the current base. SiLU replaced GELU for -2.2% (E021), and the Triton elementwise BN+act kernels are still ~18% of GPU time. ReLU's forward is a max and its backward needs only a sign mask, so Inductor can save less and recompute nothing. Base: drafts/I131_base.py. Make one change: SiLU -> ReLU in every block, all resolutions and freeze variants. Dirac init and everything else stay as they are. Run debug_nan.py under max-autotune-no-cudagraphs on every graph (E009 lesson). Screen in ONE process with one build on seeds 3-22, against the base in the same process. Both arms get separate model instances compiled and warmed in build() with channels_last tensors, so times are valid. Report the 20-seed paired delta with SE and the offline time delta. Promote into the next stack screen (I138 or a successor) only if the price is <=0.025 pp per 1% of time saved, or if accuracy is >= base -1 SE with time <= -1.5%.
ideas.expected: Time -0.8% to -2.5%, point -1.5%: less recompute in the memory-bound BN/act backward, especially at 31x31 and 15x15. Paired accuracy -0.5 to +0.1 pp, point -0.15 pp: smooth activations usually help short Muon runs a little. A loss <=0.05 pp with time <= -1.5% supports H2.4.1 and is a near-free cut. A loss >=0.25 pp closes the activation axis at SiLU.

ideas.description: Offline analysis only; no new runs and the submission is unchanged. Restate the official-gate headroom from existing data. Pool every per-seed result for the E082-math config (c0/base arms) from the I124, I126, I127/I128, I129, I130, I132 and I133 one-process logs, plus the harness E082 seeds 0-2. Report: (1) the empirical per-seed sd; (2) the between-process sd of the per-process means, after subtracting the expected sampling sd sqrt(sd^2/n); (3) the implied distribution of a 40-seed official mean on a fresh build, with the PCIe judge treated as one more process draw. Then compute P(official mean >= 0.750) for the current tip and for a hypothetical recipe 0.2 pp lower. Use the result to set the launch-rule sd (currently 0.19) and the lowest true mean any future time cut may spend down to. Record the result in the notebook as evidence for H4.3 and H4.1.8.
ideas.expected: Per-seed sd ~0.28-0.35 pp. Between-process sd of the means ~0.05-0.08 pp, smaller than I123's 0.13 pp single-pair anecdote suggested. Grand mean ~0.7539. P(official >= 0.750) > 0.999 for the tip, and still > 0.99 at 0.2 pp lower. This would support H4.3: the local 3-seed gate, not official safety, binds. It would also tighten the launch-rule sd to ~0.17-0.18, raising P for borderline candidates by ~3-5 points. A between-process sd >= 0.12 pp would instead mean build-level kernel choices shift true accuracy, and launch rules would need a wider sd.

The queue was empty, so I added 5 new ideas: 3 exploit and 2 explore. The tip is still E082 at 4.584 s. One-process screens have now covered every tunable setting (Muon lr in every shape, momentum, SGD-group wd and momentum, augmentation, pooling, schedule, averaging). All of them are at their optimum or flat, and every time cut priced so far sits on the ~0.05 pp per 1% frontier.

What's left falls into three groups:

1. **Launch the math-preserving base (I136, priority 5).** I131_base is E082 plus a compiled lookahead blend, a whole-epoch resize, and buffers and warmups set up in build(). It should save ~1.8% (point ~4.50 s). Its pass chance on the 3-seed gate is ~0.65-0.70, given a grand mean of ~0.7540 across the seven one-process screens. Launch once, no re-roll.

2. **Test where blocks downsample (new node H8).** ConvGroup runs conv1 before its max-pool. The first convs of blocks 2 and 3 are each ~21% of FLOPs, and pooling first would cut them ~5x without changing any output or final-map size. Nobody has varied this.
   - **I137 (priority 4):** a 40-seed one-process screen pricing pool-first in block 3, blocks 2+3, block 1, and blocks 2+3 at low resolution only.
   - **I138 (priority 3):** runs only if I137 finds an arm priced at half the frontier or better. It turns that arm's saving into extra epochs, picks a config with the I130-style EV rule, and launches once.

3. **Smaller checks.**
   - **I139 (priority 2):** screens SiLU against ReLU for elementwise cost (H2.4.1).
   - **I140 (priority 1):** an offline-only analysis that pools the existing per-seed data. It restates official-gate headroom (H4.3) and calibrates the launch-rule sd.

No queued items needed dropping: everything in the queue was already done or dropped.
